beats.narration_en: Why is this giant bridge spinning above a railway?
It's a road bridge in China that was built beside the tracks.
Trains can't stop for long so it's built first and turned into place.
The whole bridge sits on one giant ball joint in its pier.
It weighs forty-six thousand tons and is almost nine hundred feet long.
Then it slowly turns on that one joint.
It swung fifty-two degrees in sixty-eight minutes.
That's about eight times slower than a clock's minute hand.
The railway gave the builders a window of under two hours.
And trains were rolling underneath again soon after.
That's why some bridges in China are built sideways and then spun into place.
